title: The Anonymous Letters
subtitle: Six letters, one hand
briefing: Fiona Kerrigan, who runs a haulage firm, has received six anonymous letters over nine weeks. They are typed, unsigned, and increasingly specific about her movements. The most recent describes the interior of her home office. The police want the sender identified before the threats escalate.
solution: Roland Petrie, the firm's bookkeeper, wrote all six. He had been moving small sums out of the accounts for three years and began the letters when Fiona commissioned an external audit. The details of her home office came from a quotation visit he made for the firm's insurance renewal. His attempt to disguise his writing failed on a spelling habit and a printer that leaves a signature.

topics.office_visit: who has been in her home office

suspects.name: Roland Petrie
suspects.motive: Three years of small unexplained withdrawals, about to be audited.

statements.question: What do you know about the letters?
statements.text: Only what Fiona has told the office. It is a dreadful business.

statements.question: Have you been in her home office?
statements.text: Never. I have not set foot in that house.

statements.question: How do you feel about the external audit?
statements.text: It is overdue, frankly. I have been asking for one for years.

suspects.name: Declan Fry
suspects.motive: Was formally warned by Fiona a fortnight before the first letter.

statements.question: What do you know about the letters?
statements.text: I heard about them in the canteen. That is all.

statements.question: Have you been in her home office?
statements.text: Once, last winter, to drop off keys. I stood in the doorway.

statements.question: How do you feel about the external audit?
statements.text: It does not touch the yard. Good luck to them.

suspects.name: Mairead Kerrigan
suspects.motive: Disagreed publicly with Fiona over selling the firm.

statements.question: What do you know about the letters?
statements.text: I have read three of them. They are written by somebody who knows the accounts.

statements.question: Have you been in her home office?
statements.text: Constantly. We do half our board business at her kitchen table.

statements.question: How do you feel about the external audit?
statements.text: I asked for it. Fiona resisted for months.

suspects.name: Bridget Nolan
suspects.motive: Opens every letter that arrives, including these.

statements.question: What do you know about the letters?
statements.text: I opened four of them. I wish I had not.

statements.question: Have you been in her home office?
statements.text: No. I have never been to the house.

statements.question: How do you feel about the external audit?
statements.text: It means more filing for me. That is my entire opinion.

timeline.text: The letters begin describing her movements.
An insurance quotation visit takes place at the house.
The sixth letter describes the interior of the home office.
The audit fieldwork is scheduled to begin.

hints: The writer tried to disguise their style but not their spelling.
Printers leave a signature. Find the machine, not the person.
Ask who had a reason to want the audit stopped.
